The first version drew Larsa, Ur and Lagash for all of -2000..-1801, double-claiming Ur with elam (-2004..-1983) and isin (-1983..-1924).] The division is this dossier's reading.

correction.text: Rim-Sin I's Larsa, which 'controlled about 10–15 other city-states' with Mashkan-shapir 'on the northern edge of Rim-Sin's realm', Pi-Naratim at the river mouths, Uruk (1801) and, from 1792, Isin; it ends with Hammurabi's six-month siege in Rim-Sin's last year, 1763, not Cliopatria's 1761

keyframe_review.note: 48,484 km2 for -1800..-1761: right in outline for Rim-Sin's kingdom; Isin's district is excluded until -1792 by the isin dossier; the end year moves to -1763.

ledger.note: 2025 BCE: Naplanum's dynasty at Larsa. 'Naplanum: r. c. 2025 – c. 2005 BC (MC)' heads the king list; Ur still ruled Sumer, so Larsa is drawn as Ur's vassal to 2004 ('After the Third Dynasty of Ur collapsed c. 2004 BC'). Later kings: Abisare (c. 1905–1894), Sumuel (c. 1894–1865), Nur-Adad (c. 1865–1850), Sin-iddinam (c. 1849–1843), Kudur-Mabuk (c. 1835–1834), Warad-Sin (c. 1834–1823), Rim-Sin I (c. 1822–1763).

2025 BCE: Larsa a subject of Ur. The Larsa page does not call Naplanum a vassal or independent ('temp. of Ibbi-Suen'); the Third Dynasty page says only that 'Some Amorites, such as Naplanum, a tribal leader and general, even held important positions in the Ur III Empire', and the Larsa page that its kings ruled 'After the Third Dynasty of Ur collapsed c. 2004 BC'. The vassal reading is this dossier's, confidence 1; mirror of third-dynasty-of-ur /ledger/5, which the reviewer found unmatched.

2004 BCE: Larsa's dynasty outlives its suzerain: 'After the Third Dynasty of Ur collapsed c. 2004 BC' the line of Naplanum continues (Naplanum to c. 2005, then Emisum). Mirror of third-dynasty-of-ur /ledger/12. Isin appointed governors over Larsa afterwards (Larsa page: 'Subsequent rulers of Isin appointed governors to rule over Larsa; one such governor was an Amorite named Gungunum'), which is not booked as a vassalage (no dates; the reviewer's thin item).

region.text: Lagash province, under Gungunum as governor

ledger.note: 1932 BCE (bridged): Larsa's governor holds Lagash province. Gungunum was 'the royally appointed governor of Larsa and Lagash province' (Isin page); his reign opens in 1932 ('When Gungunum succeeded his brother Zabaya in 1932 BC', Gungunum page, which does not mention Lagash). Mirror of isin /ledger (loss of Lagash, -1932). The first version booked Lagash with Ur at -1906; the reviewer showed it was already Gungunum's.

1923 BCE: Gungunum takes Ur and breaks with Isin. He 'eventually broke with Isin and established an independent dynasty in Larsa' and 'captured the city of Ur' (Larsa page); the Gungunum page: 'The exact year of Gungunum's capture of Ur cannot be determined with certainty, but the year names found so far suggest that it took place in either his seventh or his 10th year, i.e. 1926 or 1923 BC' (year-name 10 'definitely attested in Ur'); the later year is used. Gungunum also campaigned 'against Anshan in Elam and Malgium'. [fixer me-01: re-dated from -1906 (bridged), confidence 1 -> 2, region trimmed from Ur and Lagash to Ur, Lagash being booked at -1932.]

1865 BCE: Nippur passes from Isin. 'At some point, Nippur was also lost' (Isin page), after Abisare and Sumuel 'took steps to cut Isin completely off from access to canals'; the Umma page has Sumuel's year-name 'Year Umma was destroyed'. Year and taker bridged.

region.text: Pi-Naratim, 'the mouths of the Tigris and Euphrates'

ledger.note: 1807 BCE: Rim-Sin occupies the river mouths. He 'occupied Pi-Naratim (the mouths of the Tigris and Euphrates) around 1807 BC'; Kisurra followed 'around 1802 BC' and Der was destroyed the same year.

1801 BCE: Rim-Sin takes Uruk. 'Around 1801 BC he sacked Uruk, sparing its inhabitants'; the Uruk page lists Rîm-Anum c. 1810–1802 as the last king of Sin-kashid's line, which began c. 1865. 'The king of Isin, the ruler of Uruk, and the chief of Babylon campaigned against Rim-Sin' (undated). Uruk's dynasty needs a dossier.
1797 BCE: Rim-Sin invades Isin's territory. 'Around 1797 BC, he invaded the territory of Isin, finally seizing the capital around 1792 BC'.
1792 BCE: Rim-Sin seizes Isin; 'every year name of his rule after was named in years after the sack of Isin'. Larsa now 'controlled about 10–15 other city-states' (Larsa page).
1764 BCE: Hammurabi turns on Larsa. 'Around 1764 BC, Hammurabi turned against Rim-Sin' after Rim-Sin 'had refused to support Hammurabi in his war against Elam despite pledging his troops'.
1763 BCE: 'after a six-month siege the city fell'.

region.text: Rim-Sin's kingdom of Larsa, Ur, Uruk, Nippur, Isin and the river mouths

ledger.note: 1763 BCE: Larsa falls to Hammurabi. Rim-Sin 'ruled ... from 1823 BC to 1763 BC (MC)'; 'Rim-Sin escaped the city of Larsa after its fall but was soon found and taken prisoner and died thereafter'; 'After the defeat of Rim-Sin I by Hammurabi of Babylon, Larsa became a minor site'. The Elam page: 'Around 1760 BC, Hammurabi drove out the Elamites, overthrew Rim-Sin of Larsa'. Rim-Sin II's revolt (c. 1742–1736, 'Killed in revolt against Babylon') is a rebel episode for the babylonia dossier.

wars.name: Isin–Larsa rivalry
wars.outcome: Gungunum took Ur; Abisare and Sumuel cut Isin's canals; Nippur changed hands; Rim-Sin I seized Isin c. 1792.

wars.name: Rim-Sin's wars against the Uruk–Isin–Babylon coalition
wars.outcome: 'The king of Isin, the ruler of Uruk, and the chief of Babylon campaigned against Rim-Sin' (undated; 'Around 1808 BC, the city was so big that other cities were worried about its growth'); Rim-Sin occupied Pi-Naratim (1807), Kisurra and Der (1802) and sacked Uruk (1801).

wars.name: Hammurabi's conquest of Larsa
wars.outcome: Six-month siege; Larsa fell and Rim-Sin was captured; the whole kingdom passed to Babylon.

certainty.note: City territories and canals; 'about 10–15 other city-states' is the page's whole description of the kingdom's extent.

notes:
Split from Cliopatria's 'Sumerian City-States' row: the kingdom of Larsa, -2025..-1763, reviewing the -2000 and -1800 shapes with corrections that give it the south of Sumer, and a new keyframe for Naplanum's city (as Ur's vassal) before 2004. Cliopatria's end year -1761 is moved to -1763 (Rim-Sin's last year on both pages). Bridged at confidence 1: Lagash province with Gungunum's accession (-1932), Nippur (-1865); Gungunum's capture of Ur is dated by the Gungunum page (-1923, confidence 2). Kudur-Mabuk's family 'had Elamite names' but no page gives Elam suzerainty over Larsa. Counterparts without dossiers: Uruk under Sin-kashid (c. 1865–1802), Kisurra, Der, Malgium, Eshnunna. Larsa, Isin, Kisurra, Der are not in the gazetteer; Mashkan-shapir is not placed on the pages (north of Larsa's realm).

ME-01 FIXES (after the review): (1) vassal_start -2025 / vassal_end -2004 added, counterpart third-dynasty-of-ur, mirroring that dossier (confidence 1; the Larsa page is silent on vassalage, the Third Dynasty page has Naplanum in an important position in the empire). (2) K1 is no longer Larsa + Ur + Lagash for all of -2000..-1801: larsa_-2000 (Larsa alone), larsa_-1932 (with Lagash province) and the Cliopatria shape from -1923. (3) Lagash goes to Larsa from isin at Gungunum's accession (-1932) and Ur alone at his capture, dated -1923 by the Gungunum page (opened for this fix). (4) The Gungunum page says Larsa ruled Nippur from his 19th year (c. 1914) for a time ('Larsa's dominion over the holy city did not last very long'); the ledger's Nippur gain stays at -1865 ('At some point', Isin page) and is a known gap. (5) Not done (thin): Larsa under Isin's control before Gungunum (Larsa page: 'Subsequent rulers of Isin appointed governors to rule over Larsa') is undated and not booked as a vassalage; Mashkan-shapir as a second capital is not placed (the Mashkan-shapir page was not opened).
